title: 3 Things To Say To Students Crushed By The Pandemic pandemic/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Written for students struggling emotionally during the pandemic, this piece offers three phrases teachers can use to provide comfort without overpromising or dismissing real pain: 'It's okay to be sad,' 'It will get better,' and 'You can overcome.' Linsin argues that acknowledging sadness openly counters social-media messaging that equates unhappiness with something being wrong, and that children lack the life experience to instinctively know hard periods are temporary, making an adult's reassurance meaningful. The third phrase draws on his own memory of a teacher whose belief in him became a foundation he could build on, and he lists historical figures who overcame hardship as reinforcing examples. He closes urging teachers to see themselves as essential sources of stability and hope even when their day-to-day role feels diminished by pandemic conditions.
points: 'It's okay to be sad' is recommended to counter social-media messaging equating unhappiness with something being wrong.
'It will get better' addresses children's limited life experience, which makes hard periods feel permanent rather than temporary.
'You can overcome' draws on a teacher's personal belief in a student as a foundation the student can build resilience on.
Historical examples of people who overcame adversity are suggested as reinforcing evidence for the third phrase.
Teachers are urged to see themselves as essential sources of stability even when pandemic conditions make their role feel diminished.
quotes: Trapped and muted. Dreams shattered into pieces. Forced inside and away from the friendships that mean so much to them and the school that centers their life.
Sadness is part of living in a fallen world. It’s always with us, like a fault line running through granite batholithe.
Children don’t have the life experience to fully grasp that the pandemic is temporary. It feels to them like the end of the world, like the life they once knew is over.
Your belief in your students and what they’re capable of means everything to them. I know from experience. I had a teacher change my life because he saw something in me no one else did.
No matter. They need you more now than at any other time in your career. So I urge you, be that one teacher who sees through the forest to the fields of gold beyond.
You can offer hope and comfort by remembering the three phrases above and expressing them from the empathetic depths of your own setbacks and disappointments.
